claim: When the climb meets a repeated id (a parent cycle), path_up returns [] instead of stopping there with the path climbed so far, so the result is empty although the start id names an entry.
witness: path_up([{id:"a",parent_id:"a"}], "a", [], []) = [] (D4 path: [a]); path_up([{id:"h",parent_id:"m"},{id:"m",parent_id:"h"}], "m", [], []) = [] (D4 path: [h, m]); resume fold: the real writer's valid journal with only the header's parent_id set to the leaf id "0006" gives refuse|header (the unedited journal folds: accept|3|0006|run_finished)
notes: src/core/journal.ail:1405 `then []`. Lean: bug_P5_3_cycle, bug_P5_3_header_cycle (axioms propext, Quot.sound). Differential: 1,446 of the 5,955 call-site cases whose start names an entry. Fix `then acc` (pathUpFix) is proved: fix_P5_2, fix_P5_3 (start != ""), fix_conservative (changes nothing but the [] answers); repro/check_fix.sh applies it to a throw-away copy of the tree and repro_cycle.sh then exits 0, with the fold accepting the header-cycle journal. The fixed body's sha256 db222e4c... equals the pin src/eval/journal/reader.ail:1225 records for journal.ail's path_up, so `[]` is a change since that copy was pinned. Visible effect: only cycles that pass through the header change the fold's answer (other cycles are refused `header` with or without the fix, since the first entry is not a header). Reachability not shown: the host writer (src/tui/src/session-journal.ts:368-371) writes the header's parent_id as null and every other parent as the previous leaf, so a cycle needs an edited or corrupted file, or a future branching writer (D4 rule 4).

claim: An entry may have id "" (journal_entry_of_json accepts it) but path_up tests id == "" first, as the no-parent sentinel, so a start id "" that names an entry yields [].
witness: path_up([{id:"",parent_id:""}], "", [], []) = []; resume fold: the valid journal with only the last line's id set to "" gives journal_leaf "" and refuse|header (the same edit to "0099" folds: accept)
notes: Lean: bug_P5_3_empty_id; it also shows the cycle fix does not cover this (pathUpFix gives [] too). Differential: 1,547 call-site cases. fix_P5_3_no_empty_ids: the cycle fix plus a decoder that refuses an empty id gives P5.3 for every start id; that decoder change is not tried on the real code. The cause is that "" means both 'no parent' (null or missing parent_id, journal.ail:708-711) and a legal id. Reachability not shown: the host writes ids as entryId(seq) (session-journal.ts:89-91), never empty.

claim: find_entry takes the first entry with an id while journal_leaf takes the last line's id, and nothing refuses a repeated id, so a journal whose last line repeats an earlier id is folded along a path that skips its last lines, with no refusal.
witness: path_up([{id:"a",parent_id:"",seq:0},{id:"a",parent_id:"",seq:1}], "a", [], []) = [seq 0]; resume fold: the valid journal with the run_finished line's id changed from "0006" to "0004" (the assistant history_appended's id) gives accept|3|0004|open:history_appended instead of accept|3|0006|run_finished
notes: Observation, not a registered-property violation: P5.1-P5.3 hold (the last entry does have the start id). Lean: obs_duplicate_id_first_wins. Whether a repeated id should be refused (D1 only says ids are host-assigned and opaque, ADR-003:258) is a decision about intent. Not shown reachable: the host assigns entryId(seq). Repro exits 0 once the fold refuses such a journal.

claim: Each climb step rescans the entry list from its start (find_entry) and the seen list (contains_string), so path_up costs time quadratic in the path length: on a linear 2,000-entry journal it takes about 13.5 s of CPU, 16 times the 500-entry cost.
witness: a linear journal e0..e{n-1} in file order, e_i.parent_id = e_{i-1}, climbed from e{n-1}; n = 500 vs n = 2000 (climb CPU 846 ms vs 13,496 ms; ratio 15.9 for 4x the path, after subtracting a no-climb baseline of ~210 ms)
notes: Measured on ailang v0.54.14 (CPU of the ailang process; wall-clock series in repro/scale_timings_wallclock.txt: n=3000 took 69 s). The fold runs once per resume (src/core/rpc.ail:553-557). The comment at journal.ail:1402, 'Recursion depth is the PATH length, not the file's', is also wrong: find_entry recurses to the matched entry's file position and AILANG has no tail-call elimination (Makefile:394-398), so depth reaches path plus file length; the production ceiling of 1,000,000 (src/tui/src/runtime-process.ts:1005) keeps that from failing at realistic sizes. A timing check, so run it on an idle machine; its exit-0 side (a linear-time climb) was not exercised.
